s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of lower back pain and neurological deficits in the lower extremities following a traumatic event
salient_findings: Lower back pain and tingling sensation radiating to bilateral lower extremities
Rapid progression to bilateral lower-extremity weakness
Abnormal T2 cord signal on MRI from T8 to T9 disc level downwards to the conus medullaris
key_facts: Patient is an 18-year-old female
Patient is an experienced volleyball player, yoga practitioner, and weightlifter
Symptoms developed after the eighth surfing lesson
Initial examination showed 0/5 strength of bilateral lower extremities
Intact sensation and proprioception on initial examination
Follow-up examination showed lower-extremity strength of 1 to 2/5 on MRC scale
Positive Babinski reflex on the right
Clonus bilaterally on follow-up examination
Intact rectal sensation and bowel continence
Classified as L1 American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS) C
MRI showed abnormal T2 cord signal from T8 to T9 disc level downwards to the conus medullaris
CSF analysis was negative for inflammatory/infectious etiologies
Serum analysis was negative for inflammatory/infectious etiologies

shortlist.label: Surfer's myelopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of lower back pain and neurological deficits in the lower extremities following a traumatic event, consistent with the patient's history of surfing

shortlist.label: Spinal cord infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal T2 cord signal on MRI and acute onset of neurological deficits, suggesting a possible vascular event

shortlist.label: Traumatic spinal cord infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Traumatic event followed by acute neurological deficits, consistent with a possible traumatic spinal cord infarction

shortlist.label: Acute transverse myelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of neurological deficits and abnormal T2 cord signal on MRI, consistent with inflammation of the spinal cord

shortlist.label: Spinal cord contusion
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of neurological deficits following a traumatic event, consistent with a possible spinal cord contusion

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms developed after surfing, which is a known risk factor for surfer's myelopathy, a condition characterized by spinal cord injury due to hyperextension of the spine during surfing. The patient's MRI showing abnormal T2 cord signal from T8 to T9 disc level downwards to the conus medullaris also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Spinal cord infarction
rejected.why: There is no evidence of vascular occlusion or infarction on the spinal angiogram

rejected.label: Traumatic spinal cord infarction
rejected.why: The patient's injury does not seem to be due to a traumatic event, but rather a non-traumatic hyperextension injury

rejected.label: Acute transverse myelitis
rejected.why: The patient's CSF and serum analysis were negative for inflammatory/infectious etiologies, which are common causes of acute transverse myelitis

rejected.label: Spinal cord contusion
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with a hyperextension injury, such as surfer's myelopathy, rather than a contusion
